expectations.text: Flags that transfer()'s fromAccount and toAccount are both plain strings and can be swapped silently
expectations.evidence: "fromAccount`/`toAccount` are adjacent same-typed strings — a caller can swap them and it still compiles and runs"

expectations.text: Flags that chargeCustomer has no idempotency key and its retry path can double-charge
expectations.evidence: "a charge that actually succeeded but timed out on the response gets charged twice. Separately, Stripe redelivers webhooks at-least-once — handleWebhook has no event-ID dedup, so a redelivered invoice.paid charges the customer again"

expectations.text: Flags the catch block that returns null as swallowing the error
expectations.evidence: "catch (e) never inspects or logs e; on non-retry it just return null"

expectations.text: Flags money being held as a JS number (float) rather than integer minor units
expectations.evidence: Set-aside mentions "applyDiscount doing float arithmetic" but does not flag the architectural issue of balance/amount being held as JS numbers throughout the file

expectations.text: Flags the interpolated raw SQL in purgeCanceledAccounts
expectations.evidence: "The actual delete goes through $executeRawUnsafe with a string-interpolated timestamp"

expectations.text: Flags the non-exhaustive switch over subscription status
expectations.evidence: "Any other real Stripe status (past_due, trialing, paused, unpaid, …) updates the DB but silently does nothing to features"

expectations.text: Flags JSON.parse of the webhook body as unvalidated external input
Names the mistake as an action a person can take, not a quality of the developer
expectations.evidence: "an engineer calling this expecting clean up stale canceled accounts instead purges the whole cohort"

expectations.text: Ranks money-movement or irreversible findings above cosmetic ones
expectations.evidence: Findings ranked: #1-2 webhook/charges (money), #3 transfer (money/data), #4 purge (irreversible), #5 subscription (inconsistency)

expectations.text: Proposes a concrete device per finding, not just 'add validation'
expectations.evidence: "stripe.webhooks.constructEvent", "pass a required idempotency key", "brand the account ID types", "require olderThan (no default)", "exhaustive switch with assertNever"
